catalog_quote: 1）在古丈瓦乡话里有五个声调，分别为阴平 55，阳平 13，上声 25，去声 33，入声 41。 古丈的西南官话有 4 个声调，分别为阴平 55，阳平 13，上声 41，去声 25。 “把”在中古为上声字，根据对应规律，在古丈瓦乡话中声调应为 25，可是在瓦乡话中“把”的声调为 41，与西南官话的上声调值相同。 [MS p. 4:] ……代词系统单复数由变调表示，指示代词有三分, 大多数代词的词源不详等等。 [Translation: 1) Guzhang Waxianghua has five tones: yinping 55, yangping 13, shangsheng 25, qusheng 33, rusheng 41. The Southwestern Mandarin of Guzhang has four tones: yinping 55, yangping 13, shangsheng 41, qusheng 25. 把 is a Middle Chinese shangsheng character, so by the regular correspondence its tone in Guzhang Waxianghua should be 25, but in Waxianghua 把 has tone 41, identical to the shangsheng value of Southwestern Mandarin. (p. 4) ...singular vs plural in the pronoun system is expressed by tone change, demonstratives have a three-way split, the etymology of most pronouns is unknown, etc.]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (HAL hal-03929495, 15 PDF pages, text layer present; extracted text, no scanned). PDF p. 8 = manuscript p. 7, §三 point 1) reads exactly: "1）在古丈瓦乡话里有五个声调，分别为阴平 55，阳平 13，上声 25，去声 33，入声 41。 古丈的西南官话有 4 个声调，分别为阴平 55，阳平 13，上声 41，去声 25。" followed by the argument that 把 (MC 上声, expected 25 in Waxiang) carries tone 41, i.e. the SW-Mandarin 上声 value, so it is a loan. PDF p. 5 = MS p. 4, point 2) reads: "而从语法的角度来说，瓦乡话的子尾还处于小称的阶段；……代词系统单复数由变调表示，指示代词有三分, 大多数代词的词源不详等等。" Both passages match the reported quote (only a line break and a half-width comma differ). The surrounding section is a sociolinguistic/typological sketch (§一 瓦乡话简介) and a syntax study of 跟/把 disposal marking; there is no phonology…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Waxianghua is a tone language with five lexical tones per syllable (Guzhang: 55, 13, 25, 33, 41; cf. Wu & Shen 2010 as summarized in zh-Wikipedia: Maxipu 55, 13, 35, 22, 53). None of the accessible sources makes any statement about word stress; the primary description (Wu & Shen 2010) has sections only for citation tones (单字调) and tone sandhi (连读变调) per its table of contents. The companion English paper (Chappell, Peyraube & Wu 2011, MS p. 2) says only 'Like most Sinitic languages, it is tonal'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Prosodic remarks short of a stress rule: tone sandhi marks pronoun plurality and other grammatical categories (Chappell & Wu 2009 p. 4; Chappell 2012 slide 21); clause-final markers ti 嘚 and la 啦 are 'atonal' (Chappell 2012 slide 64); a 1991 Festschrift article on Waxianghua (snippet only) says 连读变调较多,轻声也不少 ('there is much tone sandhi and neutral tone is also common'); Wang Fushi 1982 (snippet only) describes environment-conditioned tone alternation of 平声 syllables in isolation vs in compounds (Luxi variety).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation-tone inventory of monosyllables (Guzhang county variety); sandhi operates at word/compound level. No word-stress domain is defined because no stress statement exists.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog waxi1236 covers all Waxianghua/Xianghua varieties (Yuanling 沅陵, Guzhang 古丈, Luxi 泸溪, Chenxi, Xupu; Chengbu Xuntou 城步巡头 is a separate outlier described by Zheng & Peng 2016). The quoted tone statement (Chappell & Wu 2009, following Wu & Shen 2010) is for Guzhang county Waxianghua; Wang Fushi 1982, Li Guozheng 1991 and the 1991 Festschrift snippets describe the Luxi variety (4-5 tones 55/24/53/33(/42)), and Yang Wei 1999 describes Yuanling. No separate glottocodes exist for these dialects.
